svg.title: Service assurance ontology: one question, seven hops, four semantic models
svg.desc: Entity types from the Network, Enterprise services, Finance and Care semantic models, connected by relationships. The hero path runs from Incident to Site, Service-site assignment, Contract, SLA evaluation and Account, then to Account month in Finance and Case in Care. Site and Account are shared across models. Five plain-language rules govern validity periods, credit settlement, finance grain, identity and unknown values.
svg.text: Service assurance ontology: one question, seven hops, four semantic models
Each entity type keeps its source model and measures. Cross-model relationships and rules carry the meaning an agent needs to connect them.

Which enterprise customers were served from sites hit by July incidents, what SLA credit exposure do we carry on their contracts, how much revenue and margin is at stake, and who already has escalated cases?
one site_key in the Network and
per account and month, integer cents
Open cases are a daily snapshot: ask for one date, never a sum over days.
Plain language, linked to the entity types they govern. Agents read them as guidance; they are not executed.
Exposure needs overlap. The incident, the service-site assignment and the contract must be valid at the same time
Credit is settled per contract and month. Never allocate it to one incident, and apply the cap once.
Finance is per account and month. Never multiply revenue or margin across contracts or services.
Identity is the account key. Display names and billing keys are not identity.
Unknown is not zero. Report unmapped services and empty periods as exclusions.
hop on the path for the hero question
links to a source-owned DAX measure

Entity and measure names follow the Northstar sample semantic models in this repository. Graph traversal applies only to entity types bound to lakehouse or mirrored tables; over semantic models the agent plans the path and runs DAX on each model.
